body:
Please change this so that an empty command line does not set `STARSHIP_REDRAW_COUNT` to 0, so this information can be used elsewhere more easily. Though even without this change, zsh already seems to have some logic for handling this case.

Maybe also integrate `$((++STARSHIP_REDRAW_COUNT))}` directly into the starship prompt invocation.

I do not seem to understand your first suggestion. What do you mean by an empty command line?

As for your second suggestion, if I change it like this:
`--redraw-count="$((++STARSHIP_REDRAW_COUNT))"`
then it will be executed inside of subshell and variable's state won't persist.

body:
I would prefer if it also incremented the value instead of resetting to zero for empty inputs in the prompt line that don't execute anything, instead of just vi-mode switches.
This sort of thing:
```
 ❯ 
 ❯ 
 ❯ 
```
As far as I can tell, they only don't send a notification because the `STARSHIP_DURATION` variable is unset just before `STARSHIP_REDRAW_COUNT` is reset to 0.

It has been requested to reset to set the displayed status (and duration) to 0 in such cases, though that approach may not work well with any vi-mode redraw. Unlike the zsh redraw-count approach, your fish init code does increment `redraw-count` for empty lines instead of resetting it.
